comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides).
An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 — that script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions — so
nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file is what makes that check happen: on every run the script
executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to `expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different
means the condition that justified the pin has changed and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no
mechanical test exists — it is reported for manual review on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must
have an entry here, and every entry must correspond to a real pin; the script errors on either mismatch.
Prose rationale and the wider context live in AGENTS.md under 'Pinned versions'.

@codemirror/state.why: obsidian's peerDependencies names this exact version. A second copy in the tree means two CodeMirror state instances at runtime.

@codemirror/view.why: Same as @codemirror/state — obsidian peer-pins it exactly.

@lezer/common.why: Must match the copy Obsidian bundles at runtime: app.js registers '@lezer/common' in the module map it hands to plugins, so our copy is types-only and a newer pin would declare API the runtime lacks. Nothing else in the tree depends on it, so npm cannot detect or correct a mismatch. 1.5.2 was established by feature-marker comparison against Obsidian 1.13.4's app.js — see manualCheck. It replaced 1.2.3, which 1fdd8d24 had downgraded to from ^1.4.0 without a reason and which never matched the runtime.
@lezer/common.manualCheck: The check is a re-examination trigger, not proof: a newer publish means re-derive what Obsidian bundles, it does not by itself make the pin stale. The bundle embeds no version string, so derive it from feature markers — diff the dist of candidate versions (npm pack) and grep app.js for what distinguishes them. For 1.13.4: NodeProp 'combine' field and overlay 'depth++' after materialize => >=1.3.0; '-4 == size' (SpecialRecord.LookAhead) in the skipped-node scan => >=1.4.0; IterMode.EnterBracketed = 16 and MountedTree.bracketed => >=1.5.0; nextChild's bracketed test in the '!mounted.overlay && mounted.bracketed && pos >= start' form => >=1.5.1; FragmentCursor.moveTo guarding with 'cursor.to <= pos' => 1.5.2. Then run build:compile:typescript plus src/obsidian/editor.obsidian.integration.test.ts.

typescript.why: @typescript-eslint peer-requires >=4.8.4 <6.1.0, and its parser crashes on the TypeScript 7 (tsgo) native API, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7. TypeScript 7 was adopted in db7c417c and rolled back in 846d6c6a; 3234c7d0 made the pin exact so a dependency sweep could not drift it back. Propagates to the whole tree via overrides.typescript = $typescript.

js-yaml.why: js-yaml@5 drops the default export, so forcing it breaks `npm run docs:build` at Astro's own `import yaml from 'js-yaml'`. Lint and unit tests stay green, so only the docs build catches it. Held at the newest 4.x, which is the `v4-legacy` dist-tag: 4.3.1 backports the CVE-2026-59870 fix (GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj, quadratic CPU in !!omap resolution) that the vulnerable 4.0.0-4.3.0 range lacks, so this override is also what clears that advisory for astro, starlight, cosmiconfig, markdownlint-cli2 and @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config at once.
